chunks: 5602 - Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from his father, who said: My father narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: Al-Zuhrī narrated to me from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah, who said:

I sat with Ibn ʿAbbās, and the mention of the obligatory shares of inheritance was presented before me. Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent! Do you think that the One who counted the sands of ʿĀlij in number made in one estate a half, a half, and a third? These two halves have already taken the estate, so where is the place of the third?” Then Zufar ibn Aws al-Baṣrī said to him: “O Ibn ʿAbbās, who was the first to apply ʿawl to the shares?” He said: “Rumaʿ, when the shares became intertwined before him and some of them pressed against others.”

He said: “By Allah, I do not know which of you Allah has given precedence and which of you Allah has deferred, and I do not find anything broader than to divide this wealth among you according to the shares, and to enter upon every entitled person whatever enters upon him from the ʿawl of the prescribed share. By Allah, if the one whom Allah has given precedence were given precedence, and the one whom Allah has deferred were deferred, no prescribed share would undergo ʿawl.” Then Zufar ibn Aws said to him: “Which of them did Allah give precedence to, and which did He defer?” He said: “Every prescribed share which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not lowered from one prescribed share except to another prescribed share, that is what Allah has given precedence. As for what Allah has deferred, it is every prescribed share which, when it departs from its appointed share, has nothing except what remains; that is the one Allah has deferred. As for those Allah gave precedence to: the husband has a half, then if something enters upon him that removes him from it, he returns to a quarter, and nothing removes him from that. The wife has a quarter, then if she is removed from it, she becomes entitled to an eighth, and nothing removes her from that. The mother has a third, then if she is removed from it, she becomes entitled to a sixth, and nothing removes her from that. These are the prescribed shares that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave precedence to. As for those Allah deferred, the prescribed share of daughters and sisters is a half if there is one, and if there are two or more, then two-thirds. Then when the prescribed shares displace them, they have nothing except what remains; that is what Allah has deferred. So when what Allah has given precedence and what Allah has deferred come together, one begins with what Allah has given precedence, and it is given its full due. Then if anything remains, it belongs to whoever was deferred, and if nothing remains, then there is nothing for him.”

Then Zufar ibn Aws said to him: “What prevented you from indicating this view to Rumaʿ?” He said: “I stood in awe of him.” Then al-Zuhrī said: “By Allah, were it not that before him there had preceded an Imam who was just, whose conduct was upon scrupulousness, and he enforced a matter and so it went forward, no two among the people of knowledge would have differed against Ibn ʿAbbās.”

key_terms.أَعَالَ ٱلْفَرَائِضَ: applied proportional reduction to inheritance shares
key_terms.عَوْلِ ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ: the increase-based reduction affecting fixed inheritance shares
key_terms.فَرَائِضُ ٱلْمَوَارِيثِ: the obligatory legal shares of inheritance
key_terms.فَرِيضَةُ ٱلْبَنَاتِ وَٱلْأَخَوَاتِ: the prescribed inheritance shares of daughters and sisters
key_terms.ٱلزَّوْجَةُ لَهَا ٱلرُّبُعُ: the wife’s fixed inheritance share of one-quarter in the stated case
key_terms.ٱلزَّوْجُ لَهُ ٱلنِّصْفُ: the husband’s fixed inheritance share of one-half in the stated case
key_terms.ٱلْأُمُّ لَهَا ٱلثُّلُثُ: the mother’s fixed inheritance share of one-third in the stated case

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the rejection of ʿawl in inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the jurisprudence of inheritance and rejects the principle of ʿawl, the proportional reduction of fixed shares when they exceed the estate. It presents Ibn ʿAbbās’s view that some heirs have shares given precedence by Allah, while others only receive what remains after those prior shares are fulfilled.
